scope: Development evaluation on previously inspected data, not independent confirmation or ancient transfer
question: Do observed food returns improve next-departure decisions over camp-age alone?
target: Leave at the end of the final observed day of a complete camp; other days stay. Predictions at day end may use that day's returns but never later returns or total camp duration.
models: log camp age plus log last-three-day mean return relative to earlier running mean
features: age=ln(day); decline=ln((mean returns days max(1,day-2)..day +1)/(mean returns days1..max(1,day-3) +1)); decline zero before day4. The1kcal offset is numerical regularization, not physiology.
estimator: Logistic regression with L2 C=1, unpenalized intercept; training-fold StandardScaler; no class balancing; no tuned hyperparameters. Constant uses Beta(1,1) smoothed training events/exposure.
split: Leave one complete camp out; train on all other complete camps; day-weighted fitting; same eligible rows for every model.
scores: paired whole-camp bootstrap95% intervals of candidate minus baseline
adoption: Resource candidate must improve log loss against both baselines with paired bootstrap upper bound below0, and not worsen Brier score. This permits further independent evaluation only, never automatic ancient adoption.
leakage_checks: Changing future focal returns leaves earlier predictions unchanged
All feature scaling and regression exclude focal camp
limits: Observations end at departure; counterfactual return after staying is unknown
No destination selection or freshwater effect identified
Food/trade denominator and camp11 duration discrepancies retained
No threshold selected from evaluation scores
